title: Python HTTPX: Making HTTP Requests With HTTPX2
description: Learn how to use Python HTTPX (now HTTPX2) to make HTTP requests, send async calls, set safe timeouts, stream large downloads, and enable HTTP/2.
summary: If you’ve used Requests, then you’ve probably felt its limits the moment you needed to fire off a batch of API calls at once or keep one stalled server from freezing your script. HTTPX2, the Pydantic-maintained fork of Python HTTPX, keeps the Requests-style API you know while adding asynchronous requests, sensible default timeouts, and HTTP/2.
takeaways: A few things did shift in the fork: the command-line tool and the underlying httpcore package were renamed, Python 3.9 support was dropped, and TLS verification now uses your operating system’s trust store instead of a bundled certificate list.
HTTPX2, the Pydantic-maintained fork of Python HTTPX, keeps the Requests-style API you know while adding asynchronous requests, sensible default timeouts, and HTTP/2.
